title: Introduce KMS Region Consent Mediator and Pseudonymous Audit Track
author: Priya Desai
commits: c1a4e8b: add pseudonymous audit writer + rotation semantics
2d9f5e4: wire consent checks into KMS client paths
7b6d2c1: add helm templates and config values for consent mediator
5e2ab8c: add metrics and structured logging for consent decisions
a8c9f3d: tests: unit + integration harness updates
f4b77a2: docs: operations and security guidance
description:
Motivation: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions requested a mode where KMS usage is gated by explicit regional consent policies and audit logs are pseudonymized for privacy-preserving telemetry. This PR introduces a ConsentMediator component that centralizes region-based consent decisions for KMS operations, a region_resolver that deterministically maps tenant/context to a region affinity (with multi-provider fallback), and a PseudonymousAuditWriter which emits audit entries with stable pseudonyms and rotation hooks for downstream processors.

What this changes: Adds a new services/kms.ConsentMediator that is consulted by the KMS client before performing key operations. Consent decisions are logged (metrics + structured audit) and can be configured with per-tenant policy profiles (see internal/config/security.go). The region_resolver selects a primary region for routing and a fallback sequence; the ConsentMediator enforces policy delta (consent granted/denied/missing) and surfaces a machine-readable decision to callers. The PseudonymousAuditWriter implements a pluggable pseudonymization strategy: HMAC-based stable pseudonyms per-tenant+service with periodic key rotation and optional salt re-seeding for regulatory export.

Backwards compatibility: The default behavior is opt-in via helm values (deploy/helm/values-security.yaml). When disabled, KMS calls follow existing code paths. We added feature flags to enable staged rollout. No public API surface changes — the feature is internal and gated behind server-side config.

Security considerations: Consent decisions are authoritative for KMS access in this runtime; a denial results in aborting the KMS request with a structured error code (KMS_CONSENT_REQUIRED). PseudonymousAuditWriter ensures that raw identifiers are not present in logs/metrics; we retained enough context to support linking for forensic requests (via secure key escrow rotation records). The implementation is audited in code review and unit tests cover edge cases (rotation, missing keys, expired consent).

Testing and CI: Unit tests (pkg/kms, pkg/audit) added; an e2e job (integration/ci/kms-consent-e2e.yml) simulates tenant region profiles and verifies correct routing, consent enforcement, and audit output. CI summary: full test suite passing locally and on CI after two fixes (region_resolver edge-case + helm templating).

Operational notes & rollout: Start as disabled in staging, enable for a single compliance tenant using helm override values. Monitor new metrics: kms_consent_decisions_total{decision="granted|denied|missing"} and audit_pseudonym_rotate_count. If consent denials are high unexpectedly, abort rollout. There is a migration script (scripts/migrate/audit-pseudonymize-migration.sql) to seed pseudonym keys for historical entries if customers request backfilled pseudonymization.

Related work: ENG-4321 (region consent policy engine), SEC-128 (audit pseudonymization RFC). Jira SUP-7890 tracks a support request for tenant-specific consent profiles.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the ConsentMediator concurrency model (services/kms/consent_mediator.go), the deterministic nature and fallback strategy of region_resolver, and the pseudonym rotation surface in pseudonymous_writer.go. I included integration tests and a small e2e job for manual verification.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc referenced in Linear
- [x] unit tests for core components
- [x] integration e2e job added
- [x] helm and config guarded behind flags
- [x] metrics and logging added
- [x] docs for operators added

Merge strategy: squash-merge with migration plan; database migration and secret rollout must be coordinated with SRE and Customer Success for production tenants.

Priya Desai (2026-02-23): Responded: adjusted fallback order and added microbench in region_resolver_test.go; included results in commit 9b7a11f. Added note to docs about caching TTL trade-offs.

Lena Zhao (2026-02-24): Security review: the HMAC key lifecycle looks sensible, but we need an ops playbook for key rotation and emergency revocation. Requested adding a CI check that ensures rotation keys are not checked into the repo.

Priya Desai (2026-02-25): Added rotation playbook doc blurb to docs/security/pseudonymous-audit.md and a pre-commit hook entry in internal/config/security_test.go; tests assert secrets.go refuses to load dev keys from VCS. Commit c1a4e8b.

Owen Patel (2026-02-26): Approve after verifying e2e run in staging. Noted one follow-up: expose a metric for consent evaluation latency. Priya: added kms_consent_evaluation_seconds histogram in commit 5e2ab8c.

release_notes: Add opt-in KMS region consent mediator and pseudonymous audit mode. Operators should enable via helm values-security.yaml and follow rotation playbook. Backfill migration script provided for historical logs.
